place_fields.summary: A large Ranganatha temple with a sandhara garbhagriha, sukanasi, navaranga, mukhamantapa and surrounding verandah in a cloistered courtyard enclosed by a prakara wall. The temple has a south-facing mahadvara and pillared mantapas; the sanctum contains a reclining figure of Ranganatha beneath a five-hooded cobra.

planning_attributes.description: The temple is recorded as a 15th–16th century A.D. Dravidian structure built of stone, brick and mortar.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The site is documented as a 15th–16th century A.D. Dravidian temple. Its mahadvara is about 5.5 m high, and the sanctum contains Ranganatha with Sridevi and Bhudevi at the Lord’s feet.
